# One repair. Every angle.

Edition 002 — 5 October 2026. Suggested narration, about 60 seconds.

0–10s — Start near the front, with both repairs visible.
“An edit can look convincing from one camera. The next camera is where things get interesting.”

10–25s — Orbit slowly to one side, then the other.
“On the left, the repair deliberately changes with the view. On the right, the same 3D repair is projected into each image. Sharing a scene gives the views a common constraint.”

25–40s — Enable selected footprints. Change anisotropy, then lower opacity.
“These shapes are Gaussian splats. Their projected ellipses change with the camera. Their opacity decides how much of the scene behind them shows through.”

40–55s — Return to the default comparison.
“WINGS, a September 29 preprint, completes missing regions with a 3D-native prior. This is a synthetic illustration of the idea, not WINGS running or a comparison of model outputs.”

55–60s — Pause on an oblique view.
“And a consistent repair can still be wrong. Check the camera angles your shot actually needs.”

Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37816v1
Interactive: https://kavehkamali.github.io/frontier-fieldnotes/gaussian.html

Sharing: use the supplied silent MP4 for video uploads, or PNG/GIF when appropriate. The browser exports PNG/GIF from the selected controls in square or wide format. GIF is an orbit around the selected view, not a recording of your mouse movements. Keep the source and synthetic-scene label visible.
